description:
Advances: specled.tagged_tests

A tagged_tests verification's target: field is never validated against the cover ids it declares. verification_cover_untagged (tag_findings.ex:104) is the one check that reads target: and confirms the cover id is tagged in THAT file, but it filters kind in @test_file_kinds = ["test_file", "test"] — tagged_tests is excluded. So a stub may name any file, including one with no bearing on the requirement, and no finding fires at any severity. See comment for the gap analysis, the adopter impact measurement, and the two options.

comments.text:
Found while reasoning about downstream ticket builder-fnl (Builder repo), which was filed against
this library after builder-9q6.3 bounced twice on bad stub attribution. builder-fnl's own root-cause
diagnosis is partly wrong; this ticket carries the corrected scope.

## The gap, precisely

Three checks already exist and work as specified. None covers the residual case:

- specled.tagged_tests.missing_tag_finding -> tagged_tests_cover_missing_tag fires when a cover id
  has NO entry in the tag map anywhere. Works.
- specled.tagged_tests.strength_claimed_on_untagged_cover -> such a cover stays at `claimed`.
  Works, and is deliberate per the spec statement.
- verification_cover_untagged (tag_findings.ex:97-126) reads `target:` and rejects cover ids not
  tagged IN THAT TARGET FILE. Works — but only for kind in @test_file_kinds (["test_file","test"]).

The uncovered case is: **cover id IS tagged, but not in the file the stub names as `target:`.**

- missing_tag_finding does not fire (the id is in the tag map).
- verification_cover_untagged does not fire (kind == "tagged_tests" is filtered out).
- strength reaches `linked` or `executed` legitimately, via the tag map, on the strength of a test
  in a completely different file.

Net: `target:` on a tagged_tests verification is decorative. Nothing reads it for enforcement, and
nothing reports that it went unread.

Same hole at verifier.ex:809 — add_verification_target_content_findings emits
verification_target_missing_reference, also gated on `kind in @file_kinds`
(~w(file source_file test_file guide_file readme_file workflow_file test doc workflow contract)),
which likewise excludes tagged_tests.

## Why this is arguably by-design, and why it still needs a decision

For tagged_tests the real resolution path is covers -> tag_map -> files; TaggedTests.build_command/2
(tagged_tests.ex:82-106) takes only (cover_ids, tag_map) and has no legitimate need for `target:`.
That is a coherent design. The problem is that the schema still ACCEPTS `target:` on the kind, and
every human and agent reader interprets a populated `target:` as "this file is what proves it."
The field is load-bearing for comprehension and inert for enforcement — the worst combination.

Confirmed live at HEAD (0.13.0, 9adbac9c). Also present at Builder's pin (c2d21349).

## Adopter impact (measured in Builder)

Builder's spec corpus verification kind mix:

    357  tagged_tests    <- excluded from every target-honesty check
     12  test_file       <- the only kind those checks cover
    243  source_file
     40  command

~97% of Builder's test-bearing stubs are the one kind where `target:` is unenforced. Two concrete
instances inside a single epic (builder-9q6):

- 9q6.3 attempt 1 flipped kb_pinned_server_side execute:false->true against a test asserting a Mox
  relay and nothing about the KB or tool schema. Caught only by a cold audit.
- 9q6.3 as shipped still carries an inert stub (target: mcp_client_test.exs covers:
  kb_pinned_server_side) where no test in that file carries the tag. Harmless today — the
  requirement is genuinely proven elsewhere — but it reads as attribution nothing performed.

## Options

1. **Extend target-honesty to tagged_tests.** Add "tagged_tests" to the kind filter in
   verification_cover_untagged_findings/3 (tag_findings.ex:104). A stub whose target file carries
   none of its cover ids reports at the configured test_tags.enforcement severity. Smallest diff;
   reuses a finding code, severity lever, and spec requirement that already exist. Note this makes
   an existing finding newly reachable for a whole kind — expect a one-time rebaseline in every
   adopter, so it wants a release note, not a silent patch.
2. **Make `target:` structurally invalid on tagged_tests.** Reject it at schema-validate time so the
   misleading field cannot be authored. Honest, but breaks existing corpora (357 stubs in Builder
   alone would need edits) and discards genuinely useful human-facing provenance.

Recommend option 1, plus a spec requirement on specled.tagged_tests stating what `target:` means for
this kind — currently the subject spec says nothing about it, which is how the ambiguity survived.

## Sequencing note

Do NOT treat this as the fix for builder-fnl's demonstrated failure. That case (tag removed
tree-wide, stubs left claiming it) is already detected by tagged_tests_cover_missing_tag and by the
strength ladder; Builder had graded that finding to `info` and never set verification_minimum_strength
above the `claimed` floor. Builder can close its own hole in config with no upstream change. This
ticket is only the residual wrong-file-attribution case, which no configuration closes.

title: tagged_tests target: is unenforced — inert stub attribution survives every rung
